thread:
Sam: Quick post-launch check-in. Signal summary: retention on the guided prompt fell 10% vs baseline, we have a cluster of 9 regression issues (3 session aborts, 4 UX inconsistencies, 2 perf tails). Customers reporting are mostly self-serve but two mid-market accounts called out higher error rates. We need to decide what must ship as a hotpatch this sprint vs what goes into next sprint. Propose rule: hotpatch anything causing session aborts, revenue-impacting regressions, or enterprise SLA risk. Everything else = backlog. Thoughts?

Ivy: +1 to that rubric. From triage: session aborts look tied to a race in suggestions hydration on slow networks. UX inconsistencies are mostly minor layout shifts. Perf tails correlate with our new batching heuristic under bursty traffic.

Rohit: Logs show the hydration race happens when client sends duplicate init frames; quick mitigation: server-side guard to dedupe init frames (small patch) and add a client patch to debounce. Server patch estimate 0.5d, client patch 0.5d.

Tara: For the batching heuristic, short-term cap on batch latency (3ms) is feasible; deeper fix for the scheduler belongs next sprint. Cap estimate 1.0d (infra + tests).

Luis: Customer comms: the two mid-market accounts (Neptune Labs, BrightPath) are flagged as "priority". If we do an org-targeted hotpatch rollout we can notify them specifically and mitigate impact. Recommend org canary.

DeployBot: Canary template suggested: 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 3h. Auto-rollback triggers: any session-abort > 0, error-rate delta +0.4% absolute, p95 latency +300ms.

Sam: Proposed Wave 1 (hotpatch this sprint): server dedupe init frames (Rohit), client debounce (Rohit), batch latency cap (Tara), org-targeted canary for Neptune & BrightPath (Luis). Wave 2 (next sprint): scheduler refactor, UX visual polish, telemetry hardening. Approve?

Ivy: Approve. Add acceptance criteria for Wave 1: session aborts on canary = 0 over 4h, p95 <= baseline +150ms, error-rate delta <= +0.2% rolling 2h. Also require sign-off from QA before promotion.

Rohit: I'll PR the server dedupe today and the client debounce tomorrow morning. Will include unit + integration tests.

Tara: I'll implement the batch cap and add a metric to flag when requests spill into the synchronous fallback. Estimate 1d including canary wiring.

Luis: I'll draft the targeted customer note and coordinate with CS to notify Neptune Labs and BrightPath when canary starts.

QA Bot: CI snapshot: 118/122 tests passing. Will prioritize canary smoke tests and session flow E2E after PRs land.

Sam: Ops note: please avoid large infra changes during hotpatch window. Keep rollout controlled to org-based canary. We'll reserve a 2-hour status window after canary start for exec updates.

DeployBot: Health endpoint for quick checks: `curl -s -H "x-org-id: neptune" https://internal.api/health/guided_prompt | jq .ok`

Rohit: Action items recap: Rohit (server dedupe + client debounce), Tara (batch cap + metrics), Luis (customer comms & canary list), QA Bot (post-deploy smoke). Target canary kickoff: 09:00 UTC tomorrow.

Ivy: One more ask: make sure telemetry includes "init_frame_count" in canary metrics so we can validate the dedupe is effective.

Rohit: Will add metric.

Sam: Great. If canary meets acceptance criteria after 4h we'll promote and mark tickets resolved; otherwise auto-rollback and schedule a hotpostmortem. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
